\ednentry{
  id = {EDN-10},
  title = {The availability target is recovery within 30 seconds},
  note = {\textbf{Revised on 2026-11-04}: records how uptime is monitored (\#226); the target is unchanged.},
  date = {2026-09-22},
  milestone = {M6: Monitoring},
  topic = {Resource Monitoring, Requirements},
  participants = {Lukas Häußler (decided), AI agents (compared alternatives, implemented)},
  decision = {NFR-05 no longer promises 99\,\% uptime.
The API recovers by itself within 30 seconds of a crash or a reboot, which a rehearsed crash verifies.
It has no unplanned downtime during a graded presentation and its warm-up.
Outside those windows, uptime is monitored and reported, not promised: Better Stack requests the public \texttt{/\allowbreak{}health} every 3 minutes, emails the team after 3 minutes of failures, and gives a status page and the uptime figure.},
  rationale = {\emph{Alternatives considered:}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*, topsep=2pt]
\item Keep 99\,\% uptime: nothing backs it on one VM without redundancy, SLA, or on-call, and its measurement window was unbounded.
\item Lower the number to 95\,\%: as unverifiable as 99\,\%.
\item UptimeRobot: 5-minute checks. HetrixTools: little known. Freshping: shut down in 2026.
\item Uptime Kuma: self-hosted, so on the VM it cannot see the VM go down.
\end{itemize}
\par
\emph{Why:} M6 grades whether monitoring gives actionable insight, not whether a percentage was hit.
The requirement separates what we control from what we can only observe.
Better Stack is the course's tool, and its free plan covers the need.
A monitor on a URL that fails on purpose emailed 5 min 34 s after its first failing check, and the production API stayed up.},
  ai = {Information seeking, Alternative generation, Alternative assessment, Recommendation},
  response = {Accepted},
  assessment = {AI had flagged that Prometheus's \texttt{up} metric cannot see the host going down.
It proposed the requirement, compared the alternatives and wrote the setup script.
Lukas confirmed the requirement, created the account and kept Better Stack; the rehearsal was checked against the API's timeline.},
  aievidence = {Claude Code session of 2026-09-22, review of PR \#19; Lukas asked: ``what NFR that goes in the uptime direction is feasible with our system and constraints?''.
Session of 2026-11-04, AI asked (translated): ``Better Uptime (NFR-05, \#226): the API at nattech.fib.upc.edu:40520/health answers publicly, so an external check is possible. It needs a Better Stack account that only you can create. How do we do it?''
Lukas answered (translated): ``You create a free Better Stack account and put an Uptime API token into .env as BETTERSTACK\_API\_TOKEN. An agent creates the monitor, the alert (email) and the status page by API; the configuration lives as a script in the repo.''
He then asked (translated): ``Are we sure we want to use it? Is it the best for us? Or are there newer, better alternatives?''; AI answered: keep Better Stack, the course's tool.},
  evidence = {\href{https://github.com/mlops-2627q1-mds-upc/MLOPS_Recommenditos/blob/main/docs/docs/requirements.md}{Requirements} NFR-05, \href{https://github.com/mlops-2627q1-mds-upc/MLOPS_Recommenditos/blob/main/docs/docs/specification.md}{specification} NFR-05, \href{https://github.com/mlops-2627q1-mds-upc/MLOPS_Recommenditos/blob/main/docs/docs/deployment.md\#external-uptime-check}{External uptime check}, \href{https://github.com/mlops-2627q1-mds-upc/MLOPS_Recommenditos/pull/19}{PR \#19}, \href{https://github.com/mlops-2627q1-mds-upc/MLOPS_Recommenditos/issues/226}{\#226}.},
